title: Neutrophil–lymphocyte log-count coupling did not improve transported CRP prediction beyond flexible routine counts
abstract: We tested one fixed log-neutrophil × log-lymphocyte term for predicting concurrent log CRP beyond flexible marginal counts, WBC, NLR and demographic/adiposity/smoking covariates. Models trained on 4087 NHANES2005–2006 adults were frozen for 5175 separately recruited NHANES2007–2008 adults. MEC-weighted MSE changed from 1.135262 to 1.135611; baseline-minus-augmented gain -0.000349, 500 source-refit/target-resample rescaled PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-0.002533,0.000492]. No incremental benefit was established. Source cross-validation worsened; small favorable alternative-model point gains do not override the primary result. These are separate samples within one survey platform, with previously reused outcomes, not pristine independent-system clinical confirmation. A negative representation test does not exclude leukocyte biology or smaller useful effects. Autonomous AI public-data analysis and author checks; no new data collection.
